blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Learning across medical imaging modalities requires making use of images without paired text and accommodating new domains while retaining existing representations. We propose a medical vision-language technique built around an expandable bank of modality experts. Its Multiway Transformer combines shared visual computation with deterministically routed feed-forward experts and a separate text pathway. A modality-aware visual tokenizer supplies targets for masked pretraining on 19.4 million unpaired image rows across seven modalities; contrastive alignment then uses 3.23 million image-text pairs. Additional fundus and optical coherence tomography experts learn from paired data while the original image and text embedding paths remain frozen. With a ViT-Large backbone, the proposed technique achieves the best or tied-best result in 24 of 25 benchmark settings across nine modalities: 10 of 11 zero-shot classification benchmarks, all 10 linear probes, and all four retrieval benchmarks. Mean balanced accuracy is 0.674 for zero-shot classification and 0.856 for linear probing, and mean bidirectional retrieval recall is 20.70%. A separate three-seed sequential experiment with matched adaptation data yields fundus and OCT retrieval gains of 14.95 and 9.31 percentage points, with no measured loss on preceding fundus or pathology tasks. The preservation argument requires unchanged existing computation paths and inference conditions, and feature-identity checks verify retention on evaluated inputs. The proposed technique provides a modular approach to learning and expanding medical vision-language representations.

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en:
Medical representation learning must account for the visual differences among
radiography, CT, MRI, ultrasound, histopathology, dermatology, endoscopy, fundus
photography, and optical coherence tomography (OCT). A common language interface
can support text-prompted classification and image–text retrieval across these
domains, but its development faces two practical constraints. Many available
images have no paired text, and training on an additional modality can change
the representations used by existing tasks. We study an architecture that
addresses these constraints through unpaired pretraining and expandable
modality-specific capacity.

Image–text supervision alone provides an incomplete basis for this goal.
Paired medical data vary substantially across modalities, and their collection
can require expert annotation or the extraction of figure–caption pairs from
publications. The resulting training corpus need not reflect the distribution
of available clinical images. BiomedCLIP (BMC) ( Zhang et al., 2025 ) ,
the BIOMEDICA baseline (BMCA) ( Lozano et al., 2025 ) ,

These approaches motivate separating visual learning from language alignment
while extending the training scheme across medical imaging domains.

Expansion creates a second difficulty. Updating shared parameters to learn a
new modality can alter the embeddings used by existing tasks. Rehearsal and
distillation can constrain such changes ( Yao et al., 2025 ) , while progressive
architectures preserve earlier computations by freezing existing
paths ( Rusu et al., 2016 ) . For a medical vision–language encoder, this
principle must account for the image encoder, text encoder, projection heads,
and inference conditions. Preserving only a subset of these components does
not establish that previous image–text similarities remain unchanged.

blocks.en:
We introduce the proposed technique, which combines unpaired visual
pretraining with an expandable expert bank. The model builds on a Multiway
Transformer ( Wang et al., 2023a ) with a Domain-Aware Mixture-of-Experts
(DA-MoE) in the visual feed-forward layers. Each image uses a known modality
identifier to select its expert, alongside a shared visual pathway. A separate
text pathway interacts with the image encoder through contrastive alignment.
A modality-aware VQ-KD tokenizer ( Peng et al., 2022 ) supplies targets for
masked-image pretraining. The seven-modality core learns from 19.4 19.4 M unpaired
image rows and 3.23 3.23 M image–text pairs. Fundus and OCT experts subsequently
learn from paired data with the existing embedding paths frozen; the final
nine-modality assembly uses 3.34 3.34 M pairs in total across alignment and expansion.

it does not require patient-matched images across modalities. At inference,
each image is encoded through its modality route. We evaluate whether the

while earlier pathways are retained.

blocks.en: 7 Discussion and limitations
blocks.zh: 7. 讨论和限制

blocks.en:
The results support a distinction between acquiring new representations and
preserving an existing embedding function. New experts provide trainable
capacity for an added modality, while frozen original paths preserve earlier
embeddings under the conditions in Proposition 1 . Whether the
new expert reaches the strongest task performance remains an empirical
question. In the matched-data experiment, the proposed technique learns both fundus and OCT
while retaining earlier tasks, but its OCT retrieval score is below those of
the adapted baselines. Retention and new-task performance therefore need to be
assessed together.

The broader baseline comparisons do not isolate a single source of the
performance differences. Models differ in architecture, pretraining data,
parameter count, and optimization. The proposed technique uses a large bank of stored experts,
and the matched-data experiment does not match trainable parameter counts or
computational cost. The ViT-B routing and tokenizer experiments provide more
controlled evidence, but they use limited subsets and short training schedules.
Their results do not establish the size of the same effects after converged
ViT-L training.

Our expansion rule assumes that the modality is supplied at inference and
that existing preprocessing, persistent state, routing, and inference
operations remain fixed. Unchanged embeddings imply unchanged task outputs
only when scoring rules, candidate sets, and downstream classifiers are also
fixed. The feature-identity checks cover evaluated inputs. A change to the
assembled model’s learned logit-scale parameter is separate from those checks,
so preserved features do not establish identity of every scaled logit.

qualitative examples visualize similarity responses without a quantitative
localization evaluation. These experiments assess representation learning;
clinical use would require prospective validation in the intended setting.

prompting. In contrast, the proposed technique combines broad modality coverage and a language
interface within one routed encoder.

blocks.en: 9 Conclusion

blocks.en:
The proposed technique combines masked pretraining on unpaired medical images with contrastive
image–text alignment and expandable modality experts. The resulting model
supports nine imaging modalities and achieves the best or tied-best result in 24 24 of 25 25 classification, linear-probe, and retrieval settings. In a
separate matched-data sequential experiment, new experts improve fundus and
OCT retrieval while the evaluated preceding fundus and pathology tasks remain
unchanged. The preservation argument follows from retaining the original
computation paths under explicit inference conditions. Together, these results
support modular expert expansion as a way to extend medical vision–language
representations while retaining existing embeddings.

blocks.en: Domain-aware routing. All image modalities share the image-attention parameters. The text pathway uses separate attention parameters. At each routed image layer, we add the shared image FFN output to the output of the expert selected by the given modality ID: FFN ⁡ ( x , m ) = FFN shared ⁡ ( x ) + Expert m ⁡ ( x ) . \operatorname{FFN}(x,m)=\operatorname{FFN}_{\mathrm{shared}}(x)+\operatorname{Expert}_{m}(x). Here, m m denotes the image modality. Only the selected expert contributes to the layer output. However, this formulation does not claim that the implementation avoids every computation associated with unselected experts. Paired image–text training supervises the image expert; it does not add or train a modality-specific text expert.

blocks.en: Learning a new modality with a frozen text encoder. Each training pair is processed by both encoders. The image passes through the frozen shared visual pathway and the trainable expert for the new modality. The corresponding caption passes through the frozen text encoder. A contrastive loss aligns the resulting image and text embeddings. We compute text embeddings for every batch, but we do not update the text encoder. Only the image-expert FFNs for the new modality are updated. In this way, the new expert learns to map images into the existing text embedding space without requiring a new text expert.

blocks.en: Preserving existing pathways. During new-expert training, we freeze the shared visual parameters, all existing experts, the text encoder, and the projection heads. Existing modalities continue to use their original routes. When persistent state, routing, preprocessing, inference operations, scoring rules, candidate sets, and downstream classifiers also remain unchanged, the existing image and text embedding functions are preserved. The original 24-layer ViT-L core routes layers { 4 , 8 , 12 , 16 , 20 , 24 } \{4,8,12,16,20,24\} , whereas the full-data expansion model uses routed FFNs in all 24 layers. When we convert the remaining layers, FFN remapping and zero-output branches preserve the original computation for existing modalities. A new modality expert therefore contains FFN parameters at every routed layer, rather than a single FFN block. On the evaluated tasks, we verify that the saved features and predictions are bitwise identical. This is an empirical verification on those inputs, not an unconditional claim about every possible output. Scaled similarity logits need not be identical because the assembled checkpoint sequence includes a separate change to the learned logit-scale parameter.
blocks.zh: 保存现有路径。 在新专家训练期间,我们冻结了共享的视觉参数,所有现有的专家,文本编码器,以及投影头. 现有方式继续使用原有路线. 当持续状态,路由,预处理,推论操作,评分规则,候选集,下游分类器也保持不变时,保留了现有的图像和文本嵌入功能. 原为24层的VIT-L核心路由层 {4,8,12,16,20,24 }\{4,8,12,16,20,24 \};而全数据扩展模型则在所有24层中使用了路由FFN. 当我们转换出所剩的地层时,FFN再映射和零输出分支会保留对现有方式的原始计算. 因此,一个新的模式专家在每个路由层中都包含FFN参数,而不是一个单一的FFN块. 关于评估的任务,我们核实所保存的特性和预测与比特法相同。 这是对这些投入的实证核查,而不是对每一项可能的产出的无条件要求。 缩放相近的对数不需要完全相同,因为组装的检查站序列包含了对已学习到的对数尺度参数的单独更改.

blocks.en: Matched-data expansion experiment. This experiment starts from the seven-modality ViT-L checkpoint and keeps its original routed-layer structure. The 20,000 20{,}000 fundus pairs are selected from the available 88,143 88{,}143 -pair fundus training dataset, and the 16,000 16{,}000 OCT pairs are selected from the available 19,396 19{,}396 -pair OCT training dataset. We initialize the new fundus and OCT expert FFNs from the shared FFNs. At each stage, only the expert for the current modality is trainable. The shared parameters, previously trained experts, text pathway, and learned logit-scale parameter remain frozen. After selecting the fundus checkpoint, we train the OCT expert while keeping the fundus expert fixed.
